chapter.li: Verse7 And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the next day, and continued his speech until midnight. VerseEnd Verse8 And there were many lights in the upper chamber where they were gathered together. VerseEnd Verse9 And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep. And as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead. VerseEnd Verse10 And Paul went down and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves, for his life is in him. VerseEnd Verse11 When he therefore had come up again, and had broken bread and eaten and talked a long while, even until break of day, so he departed. VerseEnd Verse12 And they brought the young man alive and were not a little comforted. VerseEnd

Verse13 And we went onboard a ship and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul, for so had he appointed, intending himself to go on foot. VerseEnd Verse14 And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in and came to Mitylene. VerseEnd Verse15 And we sailed from there and arrived the next day off Chios; and the next day, we arrived at Samos and remained at Trogyllium; and the next day, we came to Miletus VerseEnd — Verse16 for Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus because he would not spend the time in Asia, for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost. VerseEnd

Verse17 And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called the elders of the church. VerseEnd Verse18 And when they had come to him, he said unto them, You know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons, VerseEnd Verse19 serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears and temptations which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews; VerseEnd Verse20 and how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have showed you and have taught you, publicly and from house to house, VerseEnd Verse21 testifying both to the Jews and also to the Greeks repentance toward God and faith on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse22 And now behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there, VerseEnd Verse23 save that the holy ghost witnesses in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me. VerseEnd Verse24 But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God. VerseEnd

Verse25 And now behold, I know that you all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more. VerseEnd Verse26 Wherefore, I take you to record this day that I am pure from the blood of all VerseEnd Verse27 men, for I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of VerseEnd Verse28 God. Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock over which the holy ghost has made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he has purchased with his own VerseEnd Verse29 blood. For I know this: that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the VerseEnd Verse30 flock. Also, of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things to draw away disciples after VerseEnd Verse31 themselves. Therefore watch, and remember that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn everyone night and day with VerseEnd Verse32 tears. And now brethren, I commend you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and to give you an inheritance among all them who are VerseEnd Verse33 sanctified. I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel. VerseEnd Verse34 Yea, you yourselves know that these hands have ministered unto my necessities and to them that were with me. VerseEnd Verse35 I have showed you all things, that so laboring, you ought to support the weak and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive. VerseEnd

Verse36 And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down and prayed with them all. VerseEnd Verse37 And they all wept severely, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him, VerseEnd Verse38 sorrowing most of all for the words which he spoke — that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship. VerseEnd

LEChapter21 Verse1 And it came to pass that after we had withdrawn from them and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from there unto Patara. VerseEnd Verse2 And finding a ship sailing over unto Phoenicia, we went aboard and set forth. VerseEnd Verse3 Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand and sailed into Syria and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload her burden. VerseEnd Verse4 And finding disciples, we remained there seven days, who said to Paul through the spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse5 And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way. And they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, until we were out of the city. And we kneeled down on the shore and prayed. VerseEnd Verse6 And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again. VerseEnd

Verse7 And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren and abided with them one day. VerseEnd Verse8 And the next day, we that were of Paul’s company departed and came unto Caesarea. And we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and abided with him. VerseEnd Verse9 And the same man had four daughters, virgins, who did prophesy. VerseEnd Verse10 And as we remained there many days, there came down from Judea a certain prophet named Agabus. VerseEnd Verse11 And when he had come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus says the holy ghost: So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this girdle and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles. VerseEnd Verse12 And when we heard these things, both we and they of that place implored him not to go up to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse13 Then Paul answered, What do you mean to weep and to break my heart? For I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. VerseEnd Verse14 And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done. VerseEnd

Verse15 And after those days, we packed our things and went up to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse16 There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple with whom we should lodge. VerseEnd Verse17 And when we had come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly. VerseEnd Verse18 And the day following, Paul went in with us unto James, and all the elders were present. VerseEnd Verse19 And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry. VerseEnd Verse20 And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord and said unto him, You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are who believe, and they are all zealous of the law. VerseEnd Verse21 And they are informed of you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs. VerseEnd Verse22 Therefore, what will be? The multitude must come together, for they will hear that you have come. VerseEnd Verse23 Do therefore this that we say to you: We have four men who have a vow on them, VerseEnd Verse24 take them and purify yourself with them, and bear the expenses with them that they may shave their heads. And all may know that those things whereof they were informed concerning you are nothing, but that you yourself also walk orderly and keep the law. VerseEnd

Verse25 As touching the Gentiles who believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication. VerseEnd

Verse26 Then Paul took the men, and the next day, purifying himself with them, entered into the temple to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until an offering should be offered for every one of them. VerseEnd

Verse27 And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews who were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people and laid hands on him, VerseEnd Verse28 crying out, Men of Israel, help! This is the man that teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place; and further, brought Greeks also into the temple and has polluted this holy place VerseEnd (Verse29 for they had seen before with him, in the city Trophimus, an Ephesian whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple) VerseEnd. Verse30 And all the city was moved.

And the people ran together, and they took Paul and drew him out of the temple, and immediately the doors were shut. VerseEnd Verse31 And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band that all Jerusalem was in an uproar, VerseEnd Verse32 who immediately took soldiers and centurions and ran down unto them. And when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul. VerseEnd Verse33 Then the chief captain came near and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains, and demanded who he was and what he had done. VerseEnd Verse34 And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude. And when he could not know with certainty, for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle. VerseEnd Verse35 And when he came upon the stairs, so it was that he was borne of the soldiers, for the violence of the people VerseEnd — Verse36 for the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him! VerseEnd

Verse37 And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto you? — who said, Can you speak Greek? VerseEnd Verse38 Are you not that Egyptian who, before these days, made an uproar and led out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers? VerseEnd Verse39 But Paul said, I am a man who is a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city; and I implore you, suffer me to speak unto the people. VerseEnd Verse40 And when he had given him license, Paul stood on the stairs and beckoned with the hand unto the people.

And when there was made a great silence, he spoke unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying, VerseEnd LEChapter22 Verse1 Men, brethren, and fathers, hear my defense which I make now unto you. VerseEnd Verse2 And when they heard that he spoke in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence. And he says, VerseEnd Verse3 I am truly a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God as you all are this day. VerseEnd Verse4 And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding, and delivering into prisons both men and women, VerseEnd Verse5 as also the high priest does bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders, from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus to bring them who were there bound unto Jerusalem to be punished. VerseEnd

Verse6 And it came to pass that as I made my journey, and had come near unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from Heaven a great light round about me. VerseEnd Verse7 And I fell unto the ground and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? VerseEnd Verse8 And I answered, Who are you, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute. VerseEnd Verse9 And they that were with me saw indeed the light and were afraid, but they heard not the voice of him that spoke to me. VerseEnd Verse10 And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise and go into Damascus, and there it shall be told you of all things which are appointed for you to do. VerseEnd Verse11 And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus. VerseEnd

Verse12 And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews who dwelled there, VerseEnd Verse13 came unto me, and stood and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive your sight. And the same hour, I looked up upon him. VerseEnd Verse14 And he said, The God of our fathers has chosen you, that you should know his will and see that Just One, and should hear the voice of his mouth; VerseEnd Verse15 for you shall be his witness unto all men of what you have seen and heard. VerseEnd Verse16 And now why do you delay? Arise and be baptized and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord. VerseEnd

Verse17 And it came to pass that when I had come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance VerseEnd Verse18 and saw him, saying unto me, Make haste and get yourself quickly out of Jerusalem, for they will not receive your testimony concerning me. VerseEnd Verse19 And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those that believed on you. VerseEnd Verse20 And when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him. VerseEnd Verse21 And he said unto me, Depart, for I will send you far from here unto the Gentiles. VerseEnd

Verse22 And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices and said, Away with such a man from the earth, for it is not fit that he should live! VerseEnd Verse23 And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air, VerseEnd Verse24 the chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bid that he should be examined by scourging, that he might know why they cried so against him. VerseEnd

Verse25 And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman and uncondemned? VerseEnd Verse26 When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what you do, for this man is a Roman. VerseEnd Verse27 Then the chief captain came and said unto him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yea. VerseEnd Verse28 And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free-born. VerseEnd Verse29 Then immediately they departed from him who should have examined him. And the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, because he had bound him. And he released him from his bands. VerseEnd

Verse30 On the next day, because he desired to have known with certainty why he was accused of the Jews, he commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down and set him before them. VerseEnd LEChapter23 Verse1 And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this VerseEnd Verse2 day. And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the VerseEnd Verse3 mouth. Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite you, you whitewashed wall, for do you sit to judge me after the law, and command that I be smitten contrary to the VerseEnd Verse4 law? And they that stood by said, Do you revile God’s high priest? VerseEnd Verse5 Then said Paul, I did not know, brethren, that he was the high priest; for it is written: You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people. VerseEnd

Verse6 But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee; of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question! VerseEnd Verse7 And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the multitude was divided; VerseEnd Verse8 for the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel nor spirit, but the Pharisees confess both. VerseEnd Verse9 And there arose a great cry, and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose and quarreled, saying, We find no evil in this man; but if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God. VerseEnd Verse10 And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain — fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them — commanded the soldiers to go down and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle. VerseEnd
Verse11 And the night following, the Lord stood by him and said, Be of good cheer, Paul, for as you have testified of me in Jerusalem, so must you bear witness also at Rome. VerseEnd

Verse12 And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul. VerseEnd Verse13 And they were more than forty who had made this conspiracy. VerseEnd Verse14 And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul. VerseEnd Verse15 Now therefore you with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you tomorrow, as though you would inquire something more perfectly concerning him; and we, before he comes near, are ready to kill him. VerseEnd

Verse16 And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle and told Paul. VerseEnd Verse17 Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain, for he has a certain thing to tell him. VerseEnd Verse18 So he took him and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him and asked me to bring this young man unto you, who has something to say unto you. VerseEnd Verse19 Then the chief captain took him by the hand and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that you have to tell me? VerseEnd Verse20 And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire of you that you would bring down Paul tomorrow into the council, as though they would inquire somewhat of him more perfectly. VerseEnd Verse21 But do not yield unto them, for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men who have bound themselves with an oath that they will neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. And now are they ready, looking for a promise from you. VerseEnd Verse22 So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See you tell no man that you have shown these things to me. VerseEnd

Verse23 And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, at the third hour of the night. VerseEnd Verse24 And provide them beasts that they may set Paul on and bring him safe unto Felix the governor. VerseEnd

Verse25 And he wrote a letter after this manner: VerseEnd Verse26 Claudius Lysias, unto the most excellent governor Felix, sends greeting. VerseEnd Verse27 This man was taken of the Jews and would have been killed of them. Then I came with an army and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman. VerseEnd Verse28 And when I desired to have known the cause for which they accused him, I brought him forth into their council, VerseEnd Verse29 whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds. VerseEnd Verse30 And when it was told me that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent immediately to you, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before you what they had against him. Farewell. VerseEnd

Verse31 Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris. VerseEnd Verse32 On the next day, they left the horsemen to go with him and returned to the castle, VerseEnd Verse33 who, when they came to Caesarea and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him. VerseEnd Verse34 And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia, VerseEnd Verse35 I will hear you, said he, when your accusers have also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall. VerseEnd

LEChapter24 Verse1 And after five days, Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who accused Paul to the governor. VerseEnd Verse2 And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by you we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by your providence, VerseEnd Verse3 we accept it always and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness. VerseEnd Verse4 Notwithstanding, that I should not be further tedious unto you, I ask that you would hear of us, of your clemency, a few words; VerseEnd Verse5 for we have found this man a pestilent man, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes; VerseEnd Verse6 who also has gone about to profane the temple; whom we took and would have judged according to our law, VerseEnd Verse7 but the chief captain Lysias came upon us and with great violence took him away out of our hands, VerseEnd Verse8 commanding his accusers to come unto you; by examining of whom, you yourself may take notice of all these things whereof we accuse him. VerseEnd Verse9 And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so. VerseEnd

Verse10 Then Paul, after the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that you have been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself, VerseEnd Verse11 because you may understand that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship. VerseEnd Verse12 And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues nor in the city; VerseEnd Verse13 neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me. VerseEnd Verse14 But this I confess unto you: that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets, VerseEnd Verse15 and have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead — both of the just and unjust. VerseEnd Verse16 And herein I do exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offense toward God and toward men. VerseEnd

Verse17 Now after many years, I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings, VerseEnd Verse18 whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple — neither with multitude nor with tumult VerseEnd — Verse19 who ought to have been here before you and object if they had anything against me; VerseEnd Verse20 or else let these same here say if they have found any evil-doing in me while I stood before the council, VerseEnd Verse21 except it be for this one voice that I cried standing among them: touching the resurrection of the dead, I am called in question by you this day. VerseEnd

Verse22 And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will examine your matter. VerseEnd Verse23 And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him. VerseEnd

Verse24 And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ. VerseEnd Verse25 And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled and answered, Go your way for this time. When I have a convenient season, I will call for you. VerseEnd (Verse26 He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might release him; wherefore, he sent for him often and communed with him. VerseEnd)
Verse27 But after two years, Porcius Festus came into Felix’s room; and Felix, willing to show the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound. VerseEnd

LEChapter25 Verse1 Now when Festus had come into the province, after three days, he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse2 Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews accused Paul to him, and implored him VerseEnd Verse3 and desired favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem (lying in wait in the way to kill him) VerseEnd. Verse4 But Festus answered that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly there. VerseEnd Verse5 Let those therefore, said he, who among you are able go down with me and accuse this man, if there should be any wickedness in him. VerseEnd

Verse6 And when he had remained among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea, and the next day, sitting on the judgment seat, commanded Paul to be brought. VerseEnd Verse7 And when he had come, the Jews who came down from Jerusalem stood round about and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul which they could not prove, VerseEnd Verse8 while he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar have I offended anything at all. VerseEnd

Verse9 But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul and said, Will you go up to Jerusalem and there be judged of these things before me? VerseEnd Verse10 Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no wrong, as you very well know. VerseEnd Verse11 For if I am an offender, or have committed anything worthy of death, I refuse not to die; but if there are none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar. VerseEnd Verse12 Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Have you appealed unto Caesar? Unto Caesar shall you go. VerseEnd

Verse13 And after certain days, king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus. VerseEnd Verse14 And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix, VerseEnd Verse15 about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him, VerseEnd Verse16 to whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die before he who is accused have the accusers face to face, and have license to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore, when they had come here, without any delay on the day following, I sat on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought forth, VerseEnd Verse18 against whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation of such things as I supposed, VerseEnd Verse19 but had certain questions against him of their own superstition and of one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive. VerseEnd Verse20 And because I was perplexed by such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem and there be judged of these matters. VerseEnd Verse21 But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept until I might send him to Caesar. VerseEnd Verse22 Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. Tomorrow, said he, you shall hear him. VerseEnd

Verse23 And on the next day, when Agrippa had come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing with the chief captains and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment, Paul was brought forth. VerseEnd Verse24 And Festus said, king Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer. VerseEnd Verse25 But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him VerseEnd — Verse26 of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore, I have brought him forth before you, and especially before you, O king Agrippa, that, after examination took place, I might have somewhat to write; VerseEnd Verse27 for it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not to signify the crimes laid against him. VerseEnd LEChapter26 Verse1 Then Agrippa said unto Paul, You are permitted to speak for yourself.

Then Paul stretched forth the hand and answered for himself, VerseEnd Verse2 I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before you, touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews, VerseEnd Verse3 especially because I know you to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Wherefore, I implore you to hear me patiently. VerseEnd Verse4 My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among my own nation at Jerusalem, all the Jews know, VerseEnd Verse5 who knew me from the beginning (if they would testify), that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived, a Pharisee. VerseEnd Verse6 And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers, VerseEnd Verse7 unto which promise our twelve tribes, earnestly serving God day and night, hope to come; for which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews. VerseEnd Verse8 Why should it be thought an incredible thing with you that God should raise the dead? VerseEnd

Verse9 I truly thought with myself that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth, VerseEnd Verse10 which thing I also did in Jerusalem. And many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them. VerseEnd Verse11 And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme.

And being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto foreign cities VerseEnd — Verse12 whereupon, as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests, VerseEnd Verse13 at midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from Heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me, and them who journeyed with me. VerseEnd Verse14 And when we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the pricks. VerseEnd Verse15 And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus, whom you persecute. VerseEnd Verse16 But rise and stand upon your feet, for I have appeared unto you for this purpose: to make you a minister and a witness — both of these things which you have seen, and of those things in which I will appear unto you VerseEnd — Verse17 delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send you, VerseEnd Verse18 to open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and inheritance among them who are sanctified by faith that is in me VerseEnd — Verse19 whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the Heavenly vision, VerseEnd Verse20 but showed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the regions of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance. VerseEnd

Verse21 For these causes, the Jews caught me in the temple and went about to kill me. Verse24 And as he thus spoke for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are beside yourself! Much learning does make you mad. VerseEnd
